models.name: Model A: ALE-based anisotropic shell FSI
models.what_it_computes: Time-resolved leaflet deformation with contact-induced coaptation, coaptation area and line pressure, peak maximum principal stress and its location, and near-valvular flow kinematics

models.name: Model B: Immersed boundary FSI with homogenized leaflet material
models.what_it_computes: Effective orifice dynamics, surrogate regurgitant fraction from backflow waveform, cycle-averaged leaflet stress, and global pressure–flow characteristics

models.name: Model C: Partitioned FSI with compliant aortic root and mortar contact
models.what_it_computes: Coupled leaflet–root motion, closure-transient load amplification, spatial stress trajectories, and coaptation contact map over the cardiac cycle

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 1: Diastolic coaptation under physiologic transvalvular pressure
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sustained seal quality determines regurgitation risk; inadequate coaptation area or line pressure compromises valve competence

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 2: Systolic opening at peak flow
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Peak leaflet stress in the open state governs durability and risk of material damage over repeated cycles

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 3: Rapid closure transient (water-hammer event)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: High-rate loading during flow deceleration can trigger transient stress spikes and flutter onset, affecting acute safety and fatigue life

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored per model–mechanism pair on a 0–100 Credibility Index, with acceptance requiring every factor score ≥ 75 and no single score < 60 for any pair.

expected_decision.outcome_source: In accordance with the predefined decision rule, the models are Not accepted for the stated context of use.

models: Model B (immersed boundary with homogenized leaflet material)
Model C (partitioned FSI with an explicitly compliant aortic root and mortar contact)
datasets: high-speed imaging with segmentation of leaflet overlap
stereo digital image correlation (DIC) on transparent leaflets
strain-to-stress conversion using material curves from planar biaxial tests
hydrodynamic loop measurements of transvalvular pressure at 5 kHz synchronized with backflow rate and leaflet kinematics
adult aortic waveform (70 bpm, 120/75 mmHg) mapping in a hydrodynamic loop
requirements: Scores of 75 or higher on all factors, with no single score below 60, are required for acceptance.

name_keywords: coaptation line load 17.2 N/m vs 18.8 N/m
peak maximum principal stress 1.42 MPa vs 1.30 MPa
estimated line load 17.0 N/m vs 18.8 N/m
cycle-averaged peak equivalent stress 1.10 MPa vs 1.30 MPa
peak maximum principal stress 1.36 MPa vs 1.30 MPa

expected_context_of_use: The context of use is preclinical design assessment of a polymeric trileaflet valve concept with edge reinforcement, where computational outputs are used to prioritize design alternatives and to screen for risk of regurgitation and material over-stress before in vitro testing.

The reinforcement strip width, measured by optical microscopy, had a mean of 0.82 mm with a standard deviation of 0.18 mm across all commissures and leaflets.

findings.mechanism: Mechanism 2: Systolic opening at peak flow
spans: Tightening nonlinear and interface tolerances by two orders of magnitude shifted key outputs by under 0.6% in sustained diastole and at peak systole, and by up to 2.2% during the closure transient in the immersed boundary solver, with similar behavior in the other models, consistent with solver residuals being subdominant contributors to errors.
findings.span: Tightening nonlinear and interface tolerances by two orders of magnitude shifted key outputs by under 0.6% in sustained diastole and at peak systole, and by up to 2.2% during the closure transient in the immersed boundary solver, with similar behavior in the other models, consistent with solver residuals being subdominant contributors to errors.

findings.mechanism: Mechanism 3: Rapid closure transient (water-hammer event)
spans: Across the three solvers and three mechanisms, halving characteristic mesh spacing and timestep altered peak principal stress by less than 3.0% for Mechanisms 1–2 and up to 3.8% for closure, and coaptation area by less than 2.3%, indicating that numerical resolution was sufficient for the questions asked.
